answer: Because the orchard index keeps every digest, the whisper audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. A 208 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, as the anchor fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 24 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
